Reproduced on reposync 826a351 and on integration 75b5499 (all fix groups merged). Scenario: tracked notes.txt "one
two
" is stat-clean (mtime in the past, update-index --refresh); the user writes .gitattributes "*.txt text eol=crlf" and stages it. git status reports only "A  .gitattributes", so Capture ships no entry for notes.txt. Restore's read-tree -u checks the index blob out under the staged attributes and writes "one
two
", while the source worktree holds "one
two
". Restore reports Exact=true with no Differences. The unstaged-.gitattributes variant passes, because applyFiles writes .gitattributes after the checkout. This is the non-LFS generalization of L0-1; reposync d5e8c0f covers only paths whose filter=lfs was dropped. A fresh mtime does not help: the text clean filter normalizes the worktree bytes back to the index blob, so status stays clean. Scratch test attached (worktree_test package, drop into reposync worktree/ to run). Decision for root/coordinator: (a) accept and document; (b) Capture compares worktree bytes against the checkout conversion (cat-file --filters) of the index blob for every path under a changed .gitattributes and ships the raw bytes when they differ; (c) Capture marks the snapshot incomplete through a named omission when a changed .gitattributes sets conversion attributes over stat-clean paths.
